_note: Practice data (key words, quiz, tricks, big ideas) for lessons whose voice script is not in the .md format that src/extract.py reads. Taken only from each lesson's own workbook text, website key facts and (7Ca) voice script in data/raw. build.py fills these fields into lessons.json data only when a lesson has none of its own, so re-running extract.py never loses them.

keywords.meaning: A living thing. You are one. A dog and a tree are too.
Moving from place to place, or moving parts.
Making more living things like yourself.
Sensing and reacting to things.
Getting bigger.
Releasing energy from food. It happens inside your cells.
Getting rid of waste. Ex means out.
Getting the substances you need to live and grow.

tricks: Mrs Gren. Each letter starts one life process: movement, reproduction, sensitivity, growth, respiration, excretion, nutrition.
bigideas: An organism is a living thing.
All organisms do the seven life processes.
Mrs Gren helps us remember them.

quiz.q: What is an organism?
quiz.a: A living thing.

quiz.q: What does Mrs Gren help you remember?
quiz.a: The seven life processes.

quiz.q: Which life process releases energy from food?
quiz.a: Respiration.

quiz.q: What does excretion mean?
quiz.a: Getting rid of waste.

quiz.q: Is respiration the same as breathing?
quiz.a: No. Breathing brings oxygen in. Respiration happens inside your cells.

quiz.q: What are the young made by reproduction called?
quiz.a: Offspring.

quiz.q: Is a car an organism?
quiz.a: No. A car cannot grow and cannot reproduce.

keywords.meaning: A large part of a plant or animal that does an important job.
The job of an organ.
A sheet of muscle under your lungs. It helps you breathe.
The science name for the gullet. It takes food from the mouth to the stomach.
The small one breaks up food and absorbs it into the blood. The large one takes water out of food.
Making food using light. It happens in the leaves.
A doctor's conclusion about what is wrong.

tricks: Good Snacks Stay Long: gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine.
Real Snails Love Flowers, from the bottom to the top: root, stem, leaf, flower.
bigideas: Every organ has a function.
Plants have organs too.
Leaves make food by photosynthesis, using light.

quiz.q: What is the function of the heart?
quiz.a: It pumps blood.

quiz.q: Which organs clean your blood and make urine?
quiz.a: The kidneys.

quiz.q: Which plant organ makes food?
quiz.a: The leaf.

quiz.q: What is a doctor's conclusion called?
quiz.a: A diagnosis.

quiz.q: What do leaves need for photosynthesis?
quiz.a: Light, carbon dioxide from the air, and water.

quiz.q: What is a storage organ?
quiz.a: A part of a plant that stores food for later, like a carrot or a potato.

quiz.q: What are the four organs of a plant?
quiz.a: Root, stem, leaf and flower. Real Snails Love Flowers.

keywords.meaning: A group of cells that are the same, all doing the same job.
A plant tissue that carries water. It is found in stems and roots.
It changes shape and moves things. In the heart, it pumps blood.
It helps roots take in water quickly.
Different tissues working together.
Organs working together.
A whole living thing.

tricks: Can Tiny Owls Sing Opera: cell, tissue, organ, system, organism.
bigideas: A tissue is a team of the same cells.
Every organ is made of different tissues.
Can Tiny Owls Sing Opera: cell, tissue, organ, system, organism.

quiz.q: What is a tissue?
quiz.a: A group of cells that are the same, all doing the same job.

quiz.q: Which tissue moves, to pump blood?
quiz.a: Muscle tissue.

quiz.q: Which tissue helps roots take in water quickly?
quiz.a: Root hair tissue.

quiz.q: Which plant tissue carries water?
quiz.a: Xylem tissue.

quiz.q: What is an organ made of?
quiz.a: Different tissues working together.

quiz.q: Put these in order, smallest first: organ, cell, organism, tissue, organ system.
quiz.a: Cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism. Can Tiny Owls Sing Opera.

keywords.meaning: A tool that makes tiny things look bigger.
The thing you look at under the microscope.
How much bigger something looks than its real size.
The control centre of the cell.
A watery jelly. Most of the cell's activities happen here.
A very thin bag. It controls what goes in and out of the cell.
Tiny jelly-bean shapes where respiration releases energy.
A large space filled with cell sap.
A green disc that makes food using light.
A cell with a special job. Its shape helps it do the job.
Made of just one cell.

tricks: Nine Cats Make Music: nucleus, cytoplasm, membrane, mitochondria.
Very Wobbly Cabbage: vacuole, cell wall, chloroplasts. The three plant extras.
Magnification: multiply, don't add. Eyepiece times objective.
bigideas: All living things are made of cells. We use a microscope to see them.
Animal and plant cells share four parts: Nine Cats Make Music. Plants have three extras: Very Wobbly Cabbage.
Some cells are specialised. Their shape fits their job.

quiz.q: Which part controls the cell?
quiz.a: The nucleus.

quiz.q: Name one part found only in plant cells.
quiz.a: The cell wall, the vacuole or a chloroplast.

quiz.q: Eyepiece ×10. Objective ×10. What is the magnification?
quiz.a: ×100. Multiply, don't add.

quiz.q: Why must a specimen be thin?
quiz.a: So light can get through it.

quiz.q: Why do root hair cells have no chloroplasts?
quiz.a: There is no light underground.

quiz.q: Which four parts do animal and plant cells share?
quiz.a: Nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane and mitochondria. Nine Cats Make Music.

quiz.q: What does unicellular mean?
quiz.a: Made of just one cell.

keywords.meaning: A group of organs that work together, to do an important job.
This system breaks down food and takes nutrients into the blood.
This system carries oxygen and nutrients around the body.
This system gets oxygen into the blood and gets rid of carbon dioxide.
This system gets rid of waste made in the body.
This system has the brain, the spinal cord and the nerves.
This system has your muscles and your bones.
A tiny piece of tissue a doctor takes, to look at under a microscope.
An unhealthy organ is replaced with a healthy one.

tricks: Can Dogs Usually Nap By Lakes? Circulatory, digestive, urinary, nervous, breathing, locomotor.
bigideas: Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, and organs make organ systems.
Your body has six organ systems. Can Dogs Usually Nap By Lakes?
Plants have a water transport system: roots, stem and leaves.

quiz.q: What is an organ system?
quiz.a: A group of organs working together.

quiz.q: Which system carries blood around your body?
quiz.a: The circulatory system.

quiz.q: Which organs are in a plant's water transport system?
quiz.a: Roots, stem and leaves.

quiz.q: What is a transplant?
quiz.a: Replacing an unhealthy organ with a healthy one.

quiz.q: What are the six body systems?
quiz.a: Circulatory, digestive, urinary, nervous, breathing and locomotor. Can Dogs Usually Nap By Lakes?

quiz.q: What is a biopsy?
quiz.a: A tiny piece of tissue a doctor takes, to look at under a microscope.

quiz.q: What does dialysis do, when the kidneys stop working?
quiz.a: A machine cleans the blood.

keywords.meaning: To make more living things of the same type.
Gone forever. There are none left anywhere, like the dinosaurs.
An idea that answers a question. You can test it with an experiment.
What you think will happen. Often: if … then …
In danger of becoming extinct.
Special sex cells. Each parent makes them.
Another name for an egg cell.
A sperm cell enters an egg cell. The two nuclei fuse.
A fertilised egg cell.

tricks: Old Queens Have Purple Elegant Dresses: observation, question, hypothesis, prediction, experiment, data.
bigideas: Scientists test ideas. Old Queens Have Purple Elegant Dresses.
In sexual reproduction, a sperm cell and an egg cell fuse.
Fish use external fertilisation. Birds and mammals use internal fertilisation.

quiz.q: What is a hypothesis?
quiz.a: An idea you can test.

quiz.q: In Redi's test, where did the maggots appear?
quiz.a: Only in the open jar.

quiz.q: What are the male and female gametes?
quiz.a: Sperm cells and egg cells.

quiz.q: What happens at fertilisation?
quiz.a: A sperm cell enters an egg cell. The two nuclei fuse.

quiz.q: What does extinct mean?
quiz.a: Gone forever. None are left anywhere.

quiz.q: What is another name for a fertilised egg cell?
quiz.a: A zygote.

quiz.q: Do fish use external or internal fertilisation?
quiz.a: External. It happens outside the body, in water.

keywords.meaning: Describes the organs where gametes are made.
It makes sperm cells. There are two.
The bag of skin that the testes hang in, outside the body.
Sperm cells and fluids from the glands.
A tube that carries urine or semen out of the body.
It releases egg cells. There are two.
The egg tube. Its other name is the fallopian tube.
Tiny hairs that sweep the egg cell along.
Where a baby develops. It has strong walls of muscle.
A ring of muscle that holds the baby in place.
When the ovaries stop releasing egg cells.
Has special features to do its job.

tricks: Make. Carry. Add. Out. The testes make sperm cells. The sperm ducts carry them. Glands add fluids. The urethra carries semen out.
Orange Owls Use Cosy Vans: the female organs, from the ovary to the outside.
bigideas: Testes make sperm cells. Make. Carry. Add. Out.
Ovaries release egg cells. Orange Owls Use Cosy Vans.
Sperm cells and egg cells are adapted to do their jobs.

quiz.q: Where are sperm cells made?
quiz.a: In the testes.

quiz.q: Why do the testes hang outside the body?
quiz.a: To keep the sperm cells cooler.

quiz.q: Which tube carries both semen and urine?
quiz.a: The urethra.

quiz.q: How does an egg cell move along the oviduct?
quiz.a: Tiny hairs called cilia sweep it along.

quiz.q: What is in the egg cell's cytoplasm?
quiz.a: A store of food.

quiz.q: What does an ovary do?
quiz.a: It releases egg cells.

quiz.q: What is the menopause?
quiz.a: When the ovaries stop releasing egg cells, usually at about 45 to 55 years old.

keywords.meaning: A baby is developing inside the woman's uterus.
The first cell of a new human. It is made at fertilisation.
A little ball of cells that grows into a baby.
The embryo sinks into the soft lining of the uterus.
One fertilised egg cell splits in two. Each cell grows into a baby.
The bag the embryo grows in.
The liquid in the bag. It cushions the embryo from bumps.
An organ shaped like a plate. It swaps substances between the two bloods.
It joins the embryo to the placenta, and carries blood to and from it.

tricks: Speedy Fish Dive In: Swim. Fuse. Divide. Implant.
The safe room: Cushion. Swap. Carry.
bigideas: Speedy Fish Dive In. Swim. Fuse. Divide. Implant.
Each parent gives half of the instructions for a new baby.
The amniotic fluid cushions. The placenta swaps. The umbilical cord carries.

quiz.q: Where does fertilisation happen?
quiz.a: In the oviduct.

quiz.q: What is implantation?
quiz.a: The embryo sinks into the soft lining of the uterus.

quiz.q: How are identical twins made?
quiz.a: One fertilised egg cell divides, and the two cells separate.

quiz.q: What does the placenta do?
quiz.a: It swaps substances between the mother's blood and the embryo's blood.

quiz.q: Why does the mother's blood not mix with the embryo's blood?
quiz.a: Her blood is at high pressure. It would damage the embryo's blood vessels.

quiz.q: What does the amniotic fluid do?
quiz.a: It cushions the embryo from bumps.

quiz.q: What is a zygote?
quiz.a: The first cell of a new human. It is made at fertilisation.

keywords.meaning: The time from fertilisation to birth. In humans it is about 9 months.
The new name for the embryo at about 8 weeks, when it has a full set of organs.
Sounds too high for us to hear. They make a picture of the foetus on a screen.
Born early and small.
Giving birth. The word means hard work.
Each squeeze of the strong muscle walls of the uterus.
The belly button. A small scar left when the stump of the umbilical cord falls off.
They make milk, in the mother's breasts.
They help to protect the baby against diseases.
Scientists who study animals.

tricks: Many Silver Vans Drive Away: medicines, smoking, viruses, drugs, alcohol. Keep them away from the foetus.
Clever Camels Always Plod Calmly Across: contractions, cervix widens, amnion breaks, push, cord is cut, afterbirth.
bigideas: Gestation is the time from fertilisation to birth. Many Silver Vans Drive Away.
Labour has six steps. Clever Camels Always Plod Calmly Across.
Zoos can breed endangered animals. Then they can return them to the wild.

quiz.q: What is the gestation period?
quiz.a: The time from fertilisation to birth.

quiz.q: When does an embryo become a foetus?
quiz.a: At about 8 weeks, when it has a full set of organs.

quiz.q: Why can smoking make a baby premature?
quiz.a: Less oxygen reaches the foetus.

quiz.q: Why did the Arabian oryx become extinct in the wild?
quiz.a: Hunting.

quiz.q: What is the first step of labour?
quiz.a: Contractions start.

quiz.q: Name two things in milk that help a baby.
quiz.a: Nutrients, for energy and growth. Antibodies, to help protect against diseases.

quiz.q: How did zoos save the Arabian oryx?
quiz.a: They bred them in a breeding programme. Then they put them back into the wild.

keywords.meaning: A time of big physical changes. The body grows fast.
Chemical messages. They travel around the body in the blood.
Spots on the skin, caused by sex hormones. It is very common.
The time when the body and the feelings change.
A monthly cycle that starts after puberty. It takes about 28 days.
The science word for a period.
When an egg cell is released from an ovary.

tricks: Happy Snails Grow Gently: hair, smell, growth, gametes. Changes in both boys and girls.
My Big Orange Moon: menstruation, build up, ovulation, menstruation again.
bigideas: Sex hormones start puberty. Happy Snails Grow Gently.
The menstrual cycle takes about 28 days. My Big Orange Moon.
Animals with short life cycles are easier to breed.

quiz.q: What starts puberty?
quiz.a: Sex hormones.

quiz.q: What is adolescence?
quiz.a: The time when the body and the feelings change.

quiz.q: How long is the menstrual cycle?
quiz.a: About 28 days.

quiz.q: What is ovulation?
quiz.a: When an egg cell is released from an ovary.

quiz.q: Why is a Sumatran rhino hard to breed?
quiz.a: It has a long life cycle, and only one calf at a time.

quiz.q: Where are sex hormones made?
quiz.a: In the brain, the ovaries and the testes.

quiz.q: What is acne, and who can help with it?
quiz.a: Spots on the skin, caused by sex hormones. A pharmacist or a doctor can help.

keywords.meaning: Keeping going for a long time without getting tired.
The rules we use to judge something.
Releasing energy from food, inside cells.
The tube that air goes in and out through. Its everyday name is the windpipe.
A muscle cell gets shorter and fatter.
Between the ribs. These muscles sit between your ribs.
A dome-shaped sheet of muscle under your lungs.
Breathing in.
Breathing out.
The air moving in and out of the lungs.

tricks: Suppleness. Strength. Speed. Stamina. Hold up four fingers, one for each S.
Inter means between. Costa means rib. So intercostal means between the ribs.
Ribs up and out. Diaphragm down. Air in.
bigideas: Fitness has four S-factors. Suppleness, strength, speed and stamina.
Breathing moves air. Respiration releases energy in cells.
Ribs up and out. Diaphragm down. Air in.

quiz.q: What are the four S-factors?
quiz.a: Suppleness, strength, speed and stamina.

quiz.q: What is respiration?
quiz.a: Releasing energy from food, inside cells.

quiz.q: What happens in gas exchange?
quiz.a: Oxygen goes into the blood. Carbon dioxide leaves the blood.

quiz.q: What does the diaphragm do when you breathe in?
quiz.a: It contracts, moves down and flattens.

quiz.q: What happens to muscles when you breathe out?
quiz.a: They relax.

quiz.q: Are breathing and respiration the same thing?
quiz.a: No. Breathing moves air. Respiration releases energy in cells.

quiz.q: Sam takes seven breaths in thirty seconds. What is Sam's breathing rate for one minute?
quiz.a: Fourteen breaths per minute.
